context.firstUser: A teacher, streamer, coach, or group host who needs a clean audience-facing draw after preparing the contestant list.
context.primaryJob: Move from setup into a distraction-free live picker on any web browser, then return to editing without losing the pool.
context.desiredResponse: Present should visibly transform the page, make the live draw dominant, and always provide an obvious exit.
referenceProducts: Wheel of Names — recognizable live-draw focus
Picker Wheel — dedicated presentation mode and enlarged picker
Kahoot — clear separation between host controls and audience-facing play

blurTest.evidence: At gallery scale, the wheel dominates, the three status controls form a clear footer band, and the exit pill remains isolated in the upper-right corner.

silhouetteTest.evidence: Presentation mode has a materially different silhouette from setup: the editor, marketing content, and site footer disappear while the stage fills the viewport.

fiveSecondTest.evidence: The user can immediately identify the live NameSnap stage, eligible count, spin action, no-repeat state, recent-pick count, and Exit view control.

realityTest.evidence: Rendered verification uses the persisted eight-person numbered pool and a real recent winner, exercising the same browser state a returning host would see.

journeyTest.evidence: The phone test entered presentation from the working setup screen, showed the stage-only state, exited through the visible control, and restored the original picker with its data intact.

platformTest.evidence: At 390×844, NameSnap uses a browser-independent in-page presentation mode; at 1440×1000, it attempts native fullscreen and preserves the same stage-only fallback if the browser drops that request.

buyerValueTest.evidence: A streamer or teacher can now turn a cluttered producer view into an audience-ready draw with one control, including on iPhone browsers that do not support arbitrary-element fullscreen.

implementationTest.evidence: Presentation state, responsive fullscreen selection, early fullscreen-drop recovery, body scroll lock, explicit exit, and regression assertions are implemented without changing native iOS source.

screenFindings.finding: The phone web view is a clean stage rather than a shrunken setup page: the wheel is centered, all core draw controls remain reachable, and Exit view is visible above the wheel.
Exiting presentation restores the setup screen and Present control without losing the saved pool.
The desktop stage scales the wheel for room visibility, retains compact live-state readouts, and removes producer and marketing surfaces from the audience view.

independentCritic.categoryFluency: PASS — the output emphasizes the actual random-draw artifact, eligible count, no-repeat state, recent winner, and primary spin action.
independentCritic.originality: PASS — NameSnap's outlined controls, lavender grid, gold-to-tan action gradient, indigo hard shadows, and numbered wheel remain intact rather than adopting a generic fullscreen overlay.
independentCritic.marketingFrameLeakage: PASS — setup copy, App Store promotion, footer navigation, and producer controls are absent from the presented stage.
independentCritic.importedCliches: PASS — the implementation uses NameSnap's own presentation language and does not introduce podium, slideshow, casino, or streaming-dashboard motifs.
independentCritic.adversarialFinding: The first automated desktop run exposed a browser that briefly accepted and then dropped fullscreen, returning to the setup page. The event handling was revised so an early browser drop preserves the stage-only fallback; the second phone and desktop renders both remained in presentation mode with a working exit.

repairs: Made Present activate a web-only stage state before requesting browser fullscreen.
Routed touch and narrow browsers directly to the in-page mode so iPhone web users are not dependent on the Fullscreen API.
Added early fullscreen-drop recovery for desktop browsers that reject or immediately leave fullscreen.
Added a prominent NameSnap-styled Exit view control plus Escape handling and scroll locking.
Added automated assertions for the responsive presentation fallback and verified entry and exit at phone and desktop viewports.
verdict: PASS — the web Present control now produces an obvious, reversible, audience-ready stage on phone and desktop while preserving the existing native iPhone app unchanged.
